_comment: L2 clarify-gate contract. The gate is deterministic (no model), it fires on ~17% of the ffmpeg corpus in the native runtime, and nothing previously proved Python's equivalent fires on the same rows. Given (utterance, plan, registry) both runtimes must produce the same post-gate payload: the plan with chain intermediates bound to their producer, or a single clarify step. Consumed by python/core/tests/test_clarify_gate_parity.py and `clarify_gate_parity_cases` in native/crates/knaif-core/tests/parity.rs.
_stage: The stage is `link_chain_intermediates -> hallucinated-filename guard`, in that order. Python composes it in CommandAgent.infer; native in knaif_core::apply_clarify_gate. Comparing either half alone would violate Rule 2. A case may declare `sandbox_files`: the filenames present in the agent's sandbox at gate time. The guard exempts a value whose STEM the user named when that value is one of those files, so both runtimes must be given the same listing to agree. Absent means an empty sandbox — nothing can be confirmed, and the strict substring rule applies.
_expected_values: Produced by the reference runtime (Python CommandAgent._link_chain_intermediates then ._hallucinated_filename). DO NOT regenerate to make a failing test pass.

cases.name: named_stem_resolving_to_a_real_file_is_not_hallucinated
cases.why: People name files the way they say them. 'downscale clip_4k to 1920x1080' names the stem; the model supplies clip_4k.mp4, the file that is actually there. Testing the full filename as a substring of the utterance overrode that correct plan with a clarify and cost the T6a control arm eight utterances across seven slices (evals/runs/2026-09-12_t6a-control_success/report.md).

cases.name: named_stem_with_an_invented_extension_still_clarifies
cases.why: Naming a stem does not license guessing which file it is. ffmpeg_228: 'join clip.mov and clip_4k together' -> the model planned clip_4k.mov, taking the extension from the other input, while clip_4k.mp4 is the file. The value names nothing that exists, so the clarify is correct - this is the case that forces the rule to check the sandbox rather than trusting the stem alone.

args.question: You didn't mention 'clip_4k.mov' in your request — which file should I work on?

cases.name: a_bare_word_is_not_a_stem_even_when_the_file_exists
cases.why: The case that decides the rule's shape. 'make the video smaller' contains 'video', and a plain stem-substring test would pass video.mp4 - a genuine hallucination - whenever such a file happened to exist. A stem must carry a structural marker (_, - or a digit), the same definition the stem resolver uses, so the guard and the resolver cannot disagree about what is resolvable.
